answer: One concrete defense: rewards vest slowly instead of paying out at once. Each new identity's earnings sit in escrow for several epochs while random peers audit its work; if audits show it shares a writing quill, so to speak, with other accounts (near-identical outputs, shared timing), the escrow is clawed back. A sybil farm can't treat the network as a safe haven to drain, because an ocean of fake accounts just means an ocean of frozen, forfeitable rewards.
